x6.title: Excursion: MATLAB structural extraction — scip-matlab or quick equivalent?
x6.imperative: One named question: is there a SCIP indexer (or quick equivalent) for MATLAB, and what structure does the best locally-available route emit from superCoolSpaceSim's matlab_src today? Human-initiated ('is there a scip Matlab or equivalent that we can test quickly?'). Brief at excursions/x6-brief.md; result at excursions/x6-result.md. Record the scoped verdict as the finding.
x6.finding: No scip-matlab exists (SCIP's 10-indexer list checked; beware name collision with SCIP Optimization Suite). But mtree wins outright: all 539 files parsed in 1.5s, zero failures, cheapest arm of the three (~21s full index). Emits 3493 transformers, 7085 named containers, 16269 call pairs, and — unlike scip-python — the WRITE side natively (17488 write occurrences; asgvars/sets/lhs built in). The MATLAB wall is resolution not parsing: 56% of qualified call sites unresolved without type inference. Feeds the extractor fork BOTH ways: AST-first gets writes for free; resolution is the hard part you own. Full: excursions/x6-result.md

x7a.title: Excursion: extractor fork candidate A — SCIP + AST sidecar prototype
x7a.imperative: One named question: can SCIP + an AST sidecar emit the statement lines for the src/utils slice, and what does the glue cost? Brief: excursions/x7a-brief.md; result: excursions/x7a-result.md. Record scoped verdict as finding.
x7a.finding: Slice extracts completely: 3,400 statements, all six predicates, 3.2s wall (index reused). Cost: 565 lines of glue, 3 debugging rounds — ALL triggered by plausible-wrong-numbers, not errors. 85% of statements needed BOTH tools. Key discoveries: the write signal is split across SCIP roles ((Definition ∪ ReadAccess) ∩ ast.Store — naive rule recovers only 9% of writes, silently); join hit 99.92% after teaching the walker SCIP's syntactic classes (imports, kwargs; residue fully explained); SCIP's 'method' kind conflates calls/imports/property-reads — 24% of naive call edges wrong, only AST disambiguates; local names come back free (93%); docstring field is hover-text needing filtering. Coupling risks ranked: silent failure modes everywhere (needs invariant assertions), two independent grammars coupled by byte offsets, wildly asymmetric refresh costs (AST 1.1s vs SCIP 6min — join must tolerate stale SCIP side), symbol identity embeds index-run version string. NOT tested: whole repo, non-ASCII, incrementality, rename identity, usefulness. Full: excursions/x7a-result.md

x7b.title: Excursion: extractor fork candidate B — AST-first prototype
x7b.imperative: One named question: can a pure-AST extractor emit the same statements for the same slice, with resolution accuracy measured against SCIP ground truth? Brief: excursions/x7b-brief.md; result: excursions/x7b-result.md. Record scoped verdict as finding.
x7b.finding: POSITIVE, hole in a different place than expected. 732-line stdlib-only extractor, zero deps, zero install, 2.3s full run (~160x faster than the SCIP path), trivially incremental, 0 parse failures. Accuracy vs SCIP ground truth: 90.4% identical on internal refs (95.6% on core slice), ZERO genuinely-wrong answers after converting confident-wrong to honest-unresolved (a wrong edge is worse than a missing edge). Writes agree 99.7%. THE REFRAME: 62.8% of qualified calls unresolved — same hole as MATLAB's 56% (x6), language-independent, a property of parse-without-inference — BUT only 46 of 3,214 (1.4%) are internal edges; the hole is almost entirely third-party dispatch. Bonus: measurement exposed FOUR SCIP defects (star-imports resolve to module stubs — 100% of x7b's apparent errors were SCIP's; third-party filed under project package name; doubled descriptors on annotated vars; aliases/builtins as anonymous locals — AST strictly better on 2,612 refs). Ground truth is an agreement bound, not truth. NOT tested: other languages (640-line resolver cost does NOT generalize to C++), whole repo, rename identity (both candidates), usefulness. Full: excursions/x7b-result.md

x8.title: Excursion: where the why lives — falsification pass over the real map
x8.imperative: One named question: does any content in f1Brainz's curated map resist living as in-code comments, and is the known-false record small? Brief: excursions/x8-brief.md; result: excursions/x8-result.md. Record scoped verdict as finding.
x8.finding: Human substantially RIGHT, one thing proves him wrong. 454 why-items classified (full corpus, no sampling): 65% single-anchor / 24% multi-anchor / 8.8% genuinely unanchorable. Known-false census: 58 records (~1 per 8 source files — small, as suspected), 84% anchor on live code ('we chose A over B' — A's function is B's obituary). THE FALSIFICATION: a known-false record's anchor is exactly what's most likely deleted — 'we built B, measured it, REMOVED it' leaves the obituary without a corpse (6 records, one mechanism; sharpest: P1b braking kernel, source deleted, record exists precisely to stop re-proposal). Two smaller resisting classes: artifact-staleness (5 — code right, stored data wrong, no line to comment) and freeze-before-look provenance (3 — the fact is a commit ordering only git proves). Decision files: 10/16 fully decompose to comments+git, 5 with small remainder, 1 not (forward roadmap for unbuilt code). Systematic loss = decision-to-code index (navigation, recoverable via stable decision-ids in comments). Bonus: 1 live map-drift found (regime_rollup OSQ row stale). Full: excursions/x8-result.md
